chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said: The worth of a man is according to his courage, his truthfulness is according to his balance of temper, his valour is according to his self-respect and his chasteness is according to his sense of shame.

key_terms.أَنَفَة: Self-respect or pride in one's status
key_terms.غَيْرَة: Sense of shame or zeal (often protective)
key_terms.مُرُوءَة: Manliness, balance of temper, or noble character

ai.seo_question: What determines a man's worth and virtue according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a profound psychological and spiritual framework in Nahj al-Balagha, linking external virtues to their internal moral engines: truthfulness stems from manliness (muru'ah), courage from aspiration (himma), bravery from self-respect (anafah), and chastity from zeal (ghayrah). This maxim reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner character (akhlaq) with outward action, suggesting that moral excellence is not merely behavioral but rooted in the depth of one's spiritual and social identity.
